name: Repainting Sun-Damaged Wood Trim on Los Angeles Homes

mainEntity.name: What special steps are needed to repaint older wood trim and fascia on Los Angeles County homes that have years of sun damage but no obvious rot?
mainEntity.text: What special steps are needed to repaint older wood trim and fascia on Los Angeles County homes that have years of sun damage but no obvious rot?

acceptedAnswer.text: On many Los Angeles County homes, fascia boards, window trim, and eaves take the brunt of sun and weather, even when there is no visible rot. Repainting these areas successfully requires more than a light scuff-sand. First, loose and flaking paint should be scraped back aggressively until only firmly bonded layers remain. Edges are then feather-sanded to reduce ridges that would show through new paint. Any greyed, UV-degraded wood should be sanded to reach a more solid surface. Small cracks, nail holes, and minor checks can be filled with exterior-grade fillers or caulk, while checking for areas that may still hide early rot. A bonding or stain-blocking primer suited for aged wood is critical to help new coatings adhere and to prevent tannin bleed-through, especially on certain species. Caulk should be applied to joints and gaps where movement occurs, using a flexible, paintable sealant. Two finish coats of a high-quality exterior paint provide UV protection and color uniformity. Ask your painter to break out wood trim prep as its own line item so you know that time and materials are allocated. Cutting corners on aged wood is one of the fastest ways to see premature peeling.
acceptedAnswer.description: Repainting sun-damaged but sound wood trim in Los Angeles County typically requires thorough scraping, sanding to bare or feathered edges, targeted repairs, high-adhesion primer, and flexible caulk. Skipping heavy prep on aged wood often leads to new paint peeling well before the rest of the exterior fails.
